title: Biscuits and Gravy
subtitle: Fluffy American biscuits smothered in pork sausage gravy
excerpt: Tall, flaky American biscuits split and drenched in a thick, peppery pork sausage gravy. A Southern diner breakfast that is filling and deeply comforting.
sourceNotes: Classic Southern American breakfast, a diner staple across the American South and Midwest.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The biscuits are best fresh from the oven. Make the gravy just before serving so it stays loose and hot.

content.text: Biscuits and gravy is the great Southern diner breakfast. The biscuits are light and flaky; the gravy is thick, peppery and full of crumbled pork sausage. Keep the butter cold for the biscuits and do not overwork the dough.

items.prepNote: very cold, cut into small cubes
removed from casings if in sausages

content.text: Heat the oven to 220C. Mix the flour, baking powder and salt in the large bowl. Rub in the cold butter until the mix looks like rough, shaggy crumbs with some pea-sized pieces still visible.
Pour in the cold milk. Stir with a fork until the dough just comes together. Do not overwork it.
Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface. Pat to 2.5cm thick. Cut out 8 rounds with a cutter or a glass. Place on the baking tray close together.
Bake for 12 to 14 minutes until risen and golden on top. While they bake, make the gravy.
Cook the sausage meat in the frying pan over a medium-high heat. Use a wooden spoon to break it into small pieces. Cook for 7 to 8 minutes until browned.
Sprinkle the flour over the sausage and stir for 1 minute so the flour absorbs the fat in the pan.
Pour in the milk gradually, whisking constantly. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes over a medium heat until the gravy is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Season with salt and plenty of black pepper.
Split the biscuits open and ladle the gravy generously over the top. Serve immediately.

items.cause: The butter was too warm or the dough was overworked.
items.fix: Use very cold butter and handle the dough as little as possible after the milk goes in.

items.cause: The milk was added too quickly.
items.fix: Add the milk in a slow, steady stream and whisk constantly so no lumps can form.

items.cause: It was cooked too long or too much flour was used.
items.fix: Add more milk a splash at a time and whisk until it loosens to a pourable consistency.
